\chapter{Not Feeling Well}
\label{ch:hi-not-feeling-well}
\hlchaptermodality{106}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say I am tired, have a cold or a cough, or am ill, and ask how someone is feeling.}

Complete HI-C106-tabiyat: say what is wrong and ask how someone feels.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[thakān]{\hi{थकान} (thakān) — tiredness}

\label{lesson:HI-C106-thakan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a fever, then the Hindi for pain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{थकान}}
\textbf{\hi{थकान}} (\emph{thakān}) — \textquotedblleft{}tiredness\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{आज} \hi{बहुत} \hi{थकान} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am very tired today\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}today there is a lot of tiredness\textquotedblright{}. The \textbf{\hi{बहुत}} and \textbf{\hi{आज}} are both yours already.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A first word for how the body feels at the end of a day.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thakān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thakān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{āj bahut thakān hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a fever, then the Hindi for pain, then say \emph{thakān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{थकान} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Tiredness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[zukām]{\hi{ज़ुकाम} (zukām) — a cold, a runny nose}

\label{lesson:HI-C106-zukam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for pain, then the Hindi for tiredness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ज़ुकाम}}
\textbf{\hi{ज़ुकाम}} (\emph{zukām}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cold\textquotedblright{}, the kind with a runny nose.

\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{ज़ुकाम} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I have a cold\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}to me there is a cold\textquotedblright{}. The person sits in \textbf{\hi{मुझे}}, as in \textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{चाय} \hi{चाहिए}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An illness, in the to-me frame you already use for wanting.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zukām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zukām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe zukām hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for pain, then the Hindi for tiredness, then say \emph{zukām} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{ज़ुकाम} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cold, a runny nose\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[khā̃sī]{\hi{खाँसी} (khā̃sī) — a cough}

\label{lesson:HI-C106-khansi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for tiredness, then the Hindi for a cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{खाँसी}}
\textbf{\hi{खाँसी}} (\emph{khā̃sī}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cough\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine.

\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{खाँसी} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I have a cough\textquotedblright{}. Same frame, new word in the middle.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A second complaint in the same frame.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khā̃sī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khā̃sī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe khā̃sī hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for tiredness, then the Hindi for a cold, then say \emph{khā̃sī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{खाँसी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cough\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bīmār]{\hi{बीमार} (bīmār) — ill, sick}

\label{lesson:HI-C106-bimar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a cold, then the Hindi for a cough.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बीमार}}
\textbf{\hi{बीमार}} (\emph{bīmār}) — \textquotedblleft{}ill, sick\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{मैं} \hi{बीमार} \hi{हूँ}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am ill\textquotedblright{}. This one describes you, so it takes \textbf{\hi{मैं} ... \hi{हूँ}}, not \textbf{\hi{मुझे}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The difference between having an illness and being ill.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bīmār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bīmār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{maiṁ bīmār hūṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a cold, then the Hindi for a cough, then say \emph{bīmār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{बीमार} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ill, sick\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tabīyat]{\hi{तबीयत} (tabīyat) — health, how one is feeling}

\label{lesson:HI-C106-tabiyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a cough, then the Hindi for ill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{तबीयत}}
\textbf{\hi{तबीयत}} (\emph{tabīyat}) — \textquotedblleft{}how one is feeling\textquotedblright{}, one's health on the day.

\textbf{\hi{आपकी} \hi{तबीयत} \hi{कैसी} \hi{है}?} — \textquotedblleft{}how are you feeling?\textquotedblright{}, the question to ask someone who has been ill. \textbf{\hi{तबीयत} \hi{ठीक} \hi{नहीं} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am not well\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The question after how are you, when you know someone has been unwell.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabīyat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabīyat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{āpkī tabīyat kaisī hai?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a cough, then the Hindi for ill, then say \emph{tabīyat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{तबीयत} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Health, how one is feeling\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
